full_judgment:
This Rule under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure arose out of the impugned judgment and decree passed by Mr M Zafar Ahmed Mina, the Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 457 of 1990, affirming the judgment and order dated 6-11-1990 passed by Assistant Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 147 of 1990, rejecting the plaint. 

 2. The plaintiff-petitioner preferred this Revisional application mainly on the grounds, among others, that both the courts below travelled beyond the plaint and based their findings upon the averments made in the application of defendant No. I which is not within the scope of Order VII rule, 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereby both the Courts below committed grave error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice; that both the Courts below failed to weigh the nature and character of the suit in the facts and circumstances of the case and committed error in holding that the jurisdiction of the Civil Court was ousted for mere presence of alternative machinery, namely, the Administrator of Waqfs; that both the Courts below failed to consider that sections 40, 81 and 102 of the Waqfs Ordinance of 1962 were not attracted in the instant case and the plaintiff did not claim any relief against any order of the Mutwalli or Administrator of Waqfs and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree are liable to be set aside. 

 4. Defendant No. 1 filed an application under Order VII rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint contending that the suit was barred by law and the plaintiffs-petitioners have no right, title and interest in getting decree for permanent injunction. After hearing both the sides the Assistant Judge, 6th Court; Dhaka rejected the plaint by order No. 6 dated 6-11-1990 with observations that plaintiffs petitioners were in possession in the suit property as tenants. Thereafter title appeal No. 457 of 1990 was filed in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka, Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka heard the appeal and recorded concurrent findings and decisions that the suit was barred by law and, as such, the Assistant Judge rightly and legally rejected the plaint. Thereafter, this Revisional application was preferred. 

 5. Muhammad Samsul Hoque, learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioners, argued supporting all the grounds of the revisional application and submits that section 102 of the Waqfs Ordinance is not attracted to the instant case and the suit was not filed against the Mutwalli or against any order of the Waqf Administrator; that if no notice was served upon the Mutwalli or Waqf Administrator before filing of the suit and in case of any decree, the Waqf Administrator may apply to the relevant court within 4(four) months for declaration that the decree is void, hence non service of notice before the institution of the suit was curable and that in paragraph 8 of the Waqf deed there are provisions for stay over the suit property even permanently by the successors of the Waqf and in that case the plaintiff-petitioners have got right, title and interest in the suit property for permanent injunction against any threat by the defendant to oust the plaintiffs from the suit property and that the Mutwali is to obey the terms, conditions and plan of the Waqf deed, when Mutwali did not obey the conditions of the Waqf deed the plaintiff-petitioners had to file the suit which is maintainable in law. 

 7. Mr Abdus Salam Khan assisted by Mr Aminul Islam Mondal, learned Advocate for the defendant-opposite parties refuted all the grounds of the Revisional application and submits that the case- laws reported in 19 DLR 775 and 27 DLR (AD) 138 are not applicable to the instant case and that the plaintiff-petitioners have no right, title and interest in the suit .and the petitioners have got possession over the suit property as tenants in the Wakf property and this does not create any right, title and interest over the suit property for getting a decree of permanent injunction. The learned Counsel for the opposite parties further submits that admittedly the suit property is the Wakf property, Mutwalli and the Administrator of Wakfs are the necessary parties and they have not been impleaded as parties to the suit and the plaintiff-petitioners have got no locus standi and no cause of action for filing the suit for permanent injunction and, as such, the court below rightly and legally rejected the plaint and the Court of appeal below committed no error of law and no failure of justice by upholding the order of the trial Court. In support of his arguments the learned Counsel for the opposite parties cited a case-law reported in PLD 1967 Dacca 190 = 18 DLR 709, Burma Eastern Limited vs Burma Eastern Employees Union and another case law reported in 41 DLR 77 Jalaluddin Ahmed vs Matiur Rahman Khan and others and submits that the plaint of the plaintiff-petitioner was barred by law. Order VII rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure is applicable to the instant case and the Assistant Judge, Dhaka rightly and legally rejected the plaint and as such the Rule is liable to be discharged with cost. 

 8. I have seen the provisions of sections 40, 81 and 102 of the Wakfs Ordinance, 1962. Section 40 provides for power of MutwaIIi to apply to the Administrator of Wakfs for any opinion, advice or clarification. Section 81 provides for issuing notice to the Administrator of Wakf with a copy of the plaint or application before institution of the suit and section 81 (3) provides that in the absence of any notice if the decree is passed then the Administrator of Wakfs may apply within 4(four) months of his knowledge for declaration that the decree is void. Section 102 is a bar to suits against the decision or order of the Administrator.
